title: A stored answer skips the model; a reused prompt opening is billed at 0.1×
aria: Two caches skip repeated model work. Above, Tunatutor's answer cache: a normalised key with no user id finds a row in panel_content_cache; a hit makes no model call, a miss calls the model, validates the answer and stores it at version 6, and two wrong-language reports delete a row. Below, the provider's prompt cache: a request with its fixed text first reuses the stored prefix at 0.1 times the input price, while a timestamp on top makes every call a miss that pays 1.25 times to write.

build.title: A learner's text becomes a key
build.text: A learner asks about a word or a sentence. Tunatutor trims and lower-cases the text, and hashes a sentence with SHA-256. No user id goes into the key, so every learner shares the row.

build.title: A stored answer skips the model
build.text: The key finds a row in `panel_content_cache` in Postgres. A hit at version 6 or later makes no model call. The learner's own words are added after the lookup and never stored.

build.title: A miss calls the model, then stores
build.text: A miss or an old version calls the model, with the fixed system prompt first. The answer is validated: a missing field stores nothing. A good answer is upserted at version 6.

build.title: Keeping stored answers right
build.text: A version bump makes every older row a miss. Two wrong-language reports from saved learners delete a row, and the next read writes it again. A semantic cache matches by meaning and can be wrong with no error, so Lomem does not use one.

build.title: The provider reuses the prompt opening
build.text: Every model call resends the whole prompt. With the fixed text first and a marker at its end, the provider keeps its work over that prefix. A hit reads it at 0.1× the input price, a miss writes it at 1.25×.

build.title: What breaks it, and how to see it
build.text: A timestamp on top makes every call a write. A prefix under the model's minimum caches nothing, with no error. The three usage counts show it. In the example day, that is $180, about $18 cached, or about $225.

route.title: Put the fixed text first and mark its end
route.text: Tools, then the 6,000-token system prompt with a `cache_control` marker at its end. The user's goal and videos, 900 tokens, go last with no marker. `ephemeral` means 5 minutes, `"ttl": "1h"` one hour.

route.title: User A misses, so the provider stores the prefix
route.text: Nothing is cached yet, so the provider processes all 6,900 tokens and keeps its work over the 6,000-token prefix. The usage says write 6,000, read 0, input 900. Storing costs 1.25× the input price.

route.title: User B hits and pays a tenth for the prefix
route.text: Within 5 minutes, user B's request starts with the same 6,000 tokens. The provider reads them at 0.1× the input price on most models and replies sooner. Every hit restarts the 5-minute clock.

route.title: Log three counts to prove it works
route.text: The usage splits input into read 6,000, write 0 and input 900. The read share is 6,000 / 6,900 ≈ 87%. It cannot reach 100% while an uncached tail exists, so 87% is healthy.

route.title: A timestamp at the top breaks every hit
route.text: The match must be exact from the first token. "Now 14:02" (made up) on top makes every prefix new, so every call pays the 1.25× write and nothing is read. Tools in a different order on each call break it the same way.
